title: Replace failed SSD and restore the image
symptom: A laptop's SSD has failed and the laptop needs a new drive and a fresh company setup
user_description: My laptop says no boot device found. The repair desk said the SSD is dead. How long until I get it back? All my work is in OneDrive, I think.

options.text: Use any system image you have, even one made for a different laptop model
options.why: An image made for different hardware can miss drivers or fail to start. Use the right image for this model.

options.text: Check where his files are backed up, fit a compatible SSD (same size and connection type, M.2 NVMe or SATA), put the company image on it with the imaging tool, restore his data, then test
options.why: The right drive, the standard company image and his restored files give him a working laptop that matches company setup.

options.text: Reinstall Windows from a USB stick and hand it straight back
options.why: Skips company apps, security settings and his data. He would not be able to work properly.

options.text: Let him use his personal laptop for work instead
options.why: Personal devices are not managed or secured by the company.

hints: Where are his files, if the old drive is dead?
Does any SSD fit any laptop?
How does the company set up a laptop the standard way?
real_world_tip: Ask him to sign in to OneDrive on the web first, to confirm his files are really there before you promise anything.
